vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — holding from July 17 evening's Vibe 4. Three concurrent signals sustain rather than shift the posture on July 18 morning. The primary de-escalation: the Iranian response 48-hour window from the July 16 CENTCOM Hellfire tanker interdiction is closing without a confirmed major Iranian counter-move. In the July 16 evening brief, the Hellfire interdiction of an Iranian tanker in Oman's territorial waters was assessed as a potential 24-48 hour Iranian response trigger. No confirmed direct Iranian surface action against US assets occurred in the window. The SNSC formal MOU void declaration remains absent (Day 4). Kharg Island oil infrastructure has not been struck. The IRGC Bab el-Mandeb activation (Houthi Red Sea closure) remains threatened but not yet executed. Iran's seventh consecutive night of horizontal retaliation — Gulf Arab state base strikes — rather than vertical escalation (Strait action, oil infrastructure) is the session's most significant restraint signal: the IRGC is testing horizontal breadth, not vertical magnitude. The primary escalation: seventh consecutive night of US strikes overnight July 17-18. The bridge/logistics interdiction arc (opened July 16-17) continues into Day 2 — CENTCOM has now operated seven strike nights across four target categories. Each successive night widening the target set rather than narrowing it signals CENTCOM is pursuing comprehensive degradation of Iranian military-logistical capability. The formal Vibe-3 drop criteria from the July 16 brief remain unmet: Kharg Island oil infrastructure not struck; no direct US-Iran surface engagement in the Strait confirmed; SNSC void declaration absent; WTI estimated ~$81-83, below the $85 sustained Vibe-3 trigger. The primary domestic positive: B and O Fire 100% containment confirmed in the July 17 evening ICS-209 — the 2026 PNW season's fastest major containment arc (0% to 100% in 8 days during east Cascades onset period). The PNW negative: a new wildfire outbreak has emerged in eastern Oregon and Washington following a lightning strike cluster after the prior heat event. Dozens of new fires across eastern OR and WA, with smoke creating hazardous AQI conditions reported by 50+ EPA monitors. The new outbreak arrives as the WA DNR Eastern Washington Burn Ban enters Day 2. Lebanon Pilot Zones (Rome Agreement, July 16) enter Day 2 with no IDF movement on Day 1 — the most stabilizing signal in the Israel-Lebanon thread since the agreement's announcement. The World Cup Final is T-1 (Spain vs Argentina, July 19, MetLife Stadium) — NIFC-FIFA co-response posture enters maximum alert for the highest-attendance event of the 2026 arc. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: Lebanon Pilot Zones confirms Day 2 no IDF movement + any credible diplomatic channel for Iran-US contact re-opens + WTI declining below $76 + eastern OR/WA new fire outbreak contained without mass evacuation. Maintain Vibe 4 requires: blockade continues without Strait-closing; Kharg Island operation not executed; CISA Day 77 streak holds; Iran restraint continues through Day 4 SNSC void declaration absent; WTI below $85 sustained. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: WTI sustained above $85; bridge strikes confirmed to include oil export infrastructure; IRGC Bab el-Mandeb activation (Houthi Red Sea closure); Hezbollah mobilization confirmed; new PNW fires produce mass-casualty or 10,000+ evacuation event. Drop to Vibe 2 requires: Kharg Island Marine landing confirmed executed; direct US-Iran ground combat confirmed; Kharg oil infrastructure struck; Iranian SNSC formal void declaration; WTI sustained above $92.

items.summary: The July 18 morning brief opens on the seventh consecutive night of US-Iran exchanges and a strategically significant Iranian restraint signal. Two primary threads define the overnight July 17-18 period. First: the seventh consecutive US strike night. CENTCOM conducted its seventh straight overnight operation against Iran (overnight July 17-18), continuing the bridge and logistics interdiction arc opened July 16-17. Specific target attribution for the July 17-18 overnight operation is pending early-morning confirmation — early reports indicate continued bridge and logistics infrastructure targeting consistent with Day 2 of the supply-chain interdiction category. The July 7-18 strike arc now encompasses seven exchange nights and four distinct target categories: (1) Iranian coastal and southern military corridor (Bandar Abbas, Jask, Chah Bahar, Bushehr, Konarak, Abu Musa — July 7-15, maritime-denial assets); (2) Tehran-periphery command and political infrastructure (July 15-16 — command-degradation expansion); (3) bridge and logistics infrastructure (July 16-18 — supply-chain interdiction, potential Iran-Iraq border crossing interdiction); (4) Hellfire tanker interdiction (July 16, Oman territorial waters — direct maritime-enforcement action). CENTCOM's target-set expansion across seven nights is the broadest US operational scope against Iran since the conflict's initiation. Each successive night has widened the operational architecture — coastal military assets to command infrastructure to logistics backbone — signaling a systematic degradation campaign rather than a discrete pressure operation. Second: the Iranian restraint signal. The 48-hour response window from CENTCOM's July 16 Hellfire tanker interdiction — the most direct US-Iranian maritime engagement of the blockade phase — is closing without a confirmed major Iranian counter-move. Iran has not: (a) issued an SNSC formal MOU void declaration (Day 4 absent); (b) struck Kharg Island oil export infrastructure — described by Trump on July 13 as protected by 'decency'; (c) activated Houthi Bab el-Mandeb forces for a Red Sea closure (the 'oil for everyone or no one' threat from July 15, still active but not executed); or (d) conducted a direct surface engagement against US naval assets in the Strait itself. Iran's seventh consecutive retaliation pattern: Gulf Arab state base infrastructure — Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan — representing horizontal breadth (more countries, same category) rather than vertical escalation (higher-consequence category). The strategic interpretation: Iran is absorbing CENTCOM's expanding strike architecture with proportional horizontal retaliation, avoiding the vertical escalation thresholds (Strait action, Kharg oil infrastructure, Red Sea closure) that would trigger the highest-consequence US responses. The Kharg Island Marine landing remains the operationally pivotal decision. The 'within the week' authorization window per National Security Journal Pentagon sources (July 16) is now Day 3 (July 16-22). Marine contingent arrival timeline: approximately end of July per deployment reporting. Iran's disinformation operation from July 16-17 (fabricated captured-Marines footage) assessed as psychological warfare to deter the operation — confirms the actual landing has not yet occurred. CNN reporting indicates Iran has layered MANPADs and air defenses on Kharg Island. The IRGC's 'oil for everyone or no one' threat continues: Houthi activation for Bab el-Mandeb closure would simultaneously shut the Red Sea and Persian Gulf routes for Gulf Arab state energy exports — the maximum Iranian leverage reserve, held but not yet deployed. Iran FM Baghaei's July 16 'no plans for negotiations' statement remains the operative diplomatic position.

items.summary: Five secondary geopolitical threads on July 18 morning. First: Lebanon Pilot Zones Day 2. The Rome Talks July 16 pilot zones agreement — establishing a south Lebanon buffer zone administration framework between Israel and Lebanon — is the most consequential Israel-Lebanon diplomatic development since the May 16 ceasefire extension. Day 1 (July 17) passed without IDF movement into the designated pilot zones — the operative test. Day 2 (July 18) monitoring: does the IDF maintain posture through the Saturday window with no movement? The Oman mediation channel (destroyed July 16 by IRGC radar strike) remains absent on Day 3, creating sustained ambiguity about Hezbollah's sanctioning posture. Without the Muscat back-channel, any Lebanon escalation would lack an Iran-Hezbollah diplomatic communication route. The Lebanon Fragile Hold extends to Day 33 — the longest sustained non-escalation period of the 2026 Lebanon arc. Second: World Cup Final T-1. Spain vs Argentina plays July 19 at 3 PM ET at MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford NJ, approximately 82,500 capacity. The final is the highest-attendance event of the 2026 arc. NIFC-FIFA co-response posture (Day 22 today) enters maximum alert ahead of tomorrow's final. The Seattle stadium CCTV 'credible threats' activation (July 9 brief) and the full FIFA security architecture remain operative through the final. Sunday July 19 is both the World Cup Final and PNW Climate Week Day 7 (closing day). Third: Russia Omsk fuel crisis Day 18. The refinery remains 75% offline; CDU-10 destroyed, CDU-11 offline. Putin's mini-refinery authorization (at gas stations, three-month construction) is the active mitigation. The IEA dual shock — Hormuz Blockade Day 4 and Omsk Day 18 — compounds at its peak adverse point. Bridge strikes on Iran continue to raise the potential that Iran-Iraq border crossings — through which Russia supplies Iran under sanctions circumvention — are disrupted. Fourth: Venezuela earthquake Day 25 — 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing; Operation Miracle humanitarian access ongoing. Fifth: Colombia T-20 to de la Espriella inauguration (August 7). Peru T-10 to Sanchez inauguration.

items.summary: The July 18 morning economic register opens at a critical threshold: September FOMC rate hike odds approaching 70% as Warsh's three stated conditions remain simultaneously adverse for the fourth consecutive day of the blockade phase. CME FedWatch September rate hike probability is tracking near 69% (from the July 16 evening 68.8% baseline) — the highest sustained probability since the blockade's reinstatement on July 15. Warsh's three-condition framework: First condition (Hormuz normalization) is maximally adverse — blockade Day 4, seven exchange nights, no diplomatic channel. Second condition (Russian refining recovery) is maximally adverse — Omsk Day 18, 75% offline, mini-refinery authorization has a three-month construction timeline (Q4 2026 earliest relief). Third condition (commodity relief) is in adverse territory — WTI estimated at $81-83, Brent $85-87, both above the $72 normalization floor and approaching the $85 Vibe-3 trigger, but the absence of Iranian escalation to Strait-closing or Bab el-Mandeb activation has prevented the price surge that a vertical escalation would trigger. The oil price math: WTI's $79.39 July 16 close, plus muted bridge-strike premia, plus the Iran 48h restraint signal (negative premium), produces an estimated range of $81-83. The event risk: Kharg Island Marine landing execution would remove 90% of Iranian crude exports and take WTI above $100 — the brief's highest single-event economic risk. The IRGC Bab el-Mandeb activation (dual Strait closure) is the secondary event risk: Red Sea + Hormuz simultaneously would produce a shipping rerouting shock larger than the 2024 Houthi campaign peak. Two new economic signals from recent trading sessions add to the adverse composite. First: import prices posted a surprise gain on July 17, with costs of goods from China hitting their highest level since 2008 — signaling inflationary pressure from the tariff architecture is compounding the energy-CPI channel simultaneously. Second: the 10-year Treasury yield is falling as traders weigh the domestic economic outlook and fresh Iran strike activity — a paradoxical signal (falling yields despite elevated hike odds) that reflects the market's dual fear of both rate hikes and economic deterioration in the event of Strait closure. Jackson Hole (T-35, August 22-24) is the next major Warsh policy communications event. July CPI (releasing approximately August 14, T-28, 8 days before Jackson Hole) is the only additional inflation data point before Warsh speaks. July CPI will capture energy prices during the full WTI blockade-era range ($79-83) — structurally adverse to any dovish Jackson Hole signal unless the Iran situation de-escalates before August.

items.summary: Four secondary economic-legislative threads on July 18 morning. First: USTR Section 301 completion deadline T-2 (July 20). Two days to deadline with no finalization announced. White House bandwidth on July 18 is consumed by the seventh consecutive night of Iran strikes, Kharg Island Marine landing decision timeline, bridge targeting BDA, and World Cup Final security coordination — all generating simultaneous NSC demand. The Iran crisis does not create legal authority to extend the July 20 statute-equivalent deadline. Without sign-off on the final Section 301 structure (proposed: 12.5% on 46 countries, 10% on 15 including EU, Canada, UK, Mexico), the July 20 deadline creates a 4-day importer planning gap before Section 122 expires July 24 — the highest-risk tariff compliance window of the 2026 arc. Second: FERC AI 30-day nominal deadline TODAY (Saturday July 18). Today is the nominal deadline for the six ISO/RTOs (PJM/MISO/SPP/CAISO/ISO-NE/NYISO). Generation adequacy reports are officially due Monday July 20 — the first business day. Today (Saturday) is the formal notification day; Monday is the submission deadline. The PJM July 3 data center curtailment emergency (160 million people affected) anchors all six submissions as the operative evidence that AI large-load integration is exceeding current grid capacity planning assumptions. PNW Climate Week Day 6 (today) provides the policy forum context — the penultimate forum day runs concurrent with the FERC nominal deadline. Any early ISO/RTO voluntary submission today before the Monday deadline would provide the first formal national accounting of AI load integration readiness. Third: OBBB Law Day 19. Medicaid work requirements and SNAP restrictions active in 18 states. Aragon v. Rollins (SNAP food restriction, five states) T-13 from the July 31 SNAP effective date — no judicial resolution. Zero federal stays. The statutory collision between the OBBB mandate and federal court USDA authority ruling approaches the enforcement deadline without relief. Fourth: Reconciliation 3.0. House Republicans unveiled a $60B defense + $70B Iran war + $20B agriculture package on July 15. Senate leadership is hesitant to advance a third party-line package ahead of November midterm elections, with rank-and-file senators raising conflicting demands. Roll Call (July 17) described Congress' July sprint as 'off to a stumbling start.' The Iran war funding component ($70B) creates both a political opportunity (bipartisan support for war finance) and a political risk (Senate calendar crowding ahead of midterms). Pharma 232 T-13 (July 31 effective date): no congressional or executive modification announced.

items.summary: The July 18 morning infrastructure session opens on a structural split in the PNW wildfire picture: the season's most watched single incident achieves full containment while a new outbreak emerges across the broader eastern Oregon and Washington landscape. The B and O Fire's 100% containment was confirmed in the July 17 evening ICS-209 — the Day 8 outcome. This represents the 2026 PNW wildfire season's fastest major containment arc: 0% containment at the July 9 ignition (east Cascades onset Day 11) to 100% by Day 8 evening, in an active onset period under 4th-year drought conditions. The suppression achievement reflects the Day 5-6 Chelan Hills resource reallocation, sustained aerial suppression, favorable overnight fire weather across the July 14-17 window, and the absence of significant wind events after the July 13 perimeter expansion. Mopup phase is underway. Level 1 remains active for the Vic Smith Road corridor north of Okanogan; Level 2 remains for Dry Coulee / East Dry Coulee / Woods Hill and adjacent areas.
